sources.title: Bacterial leaf spot
sources.organization: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Agritech Portal

background.statement: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University describes tomato bacterial leaf spot as a Xanthomonas-associated disease that can affect leaves and green fruit; infected debris and seed are listed as possible sources of spread.

reported_symptoms.statement: Reported symptoms include small brown, water-soaked circular leaf spots with yellow halos; spots on green fruit may become sunken and scabby.

sources.title: Early Blight
sources.organization: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Agritech Portal

background.statement: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University identifies Alternaria solani as the causal organism of tomato early blight and notes survival in infected plant debris and spread by rain and wind.

reported_symptoms.statement: Reported symptoms include brown spots with concentric bull’s-eye rings and a yellow margin; fruit can develop brown concentric rings.

sources.title: Late blight
sources.organization: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Agritech Portal

background.statement: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University identifies Phytophthora infestans as the causal organism of tomato late blight and describes spread associated with infected debris and wind.

reported_symptoms.statement: Reported symptoms include water-soaked dark lesions on leaves and stems, rapid leaf necrosis, white sporulation on leaves, and dark-brown fruit lesions that can progress to soft rot.

background.statement: Tomato leaf mold is caused by Passalora fulva (also known by older names including Fulvia fulva and Cladosporium fulvum) and is particularly associated with high-humidity greenhouse or high-tunnel production.

reported_symptoms.statement: Pale yellow-green spots may appear on the upper leaf surface, with olive-green to brown velvety growth on the corresponding underside; affected leaves may wither and die.

sources.title: Septoria Leaf Spot
sources.organization: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Agritech Portal

background.statement: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University identifies Septoria lycopersici as the cause of Septoria leaf spot and describes infected plant debris and rain splash or wind as spread pathways.

reported_symptoms.statement: Reported symptoms include small round-to-irregular leaf spots with grey centers and dark margins; spots may coalesce and cause blighting.

sources.title: Red spider mite: Tetranychus spp.
sources.organization: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Agritech Portal

background.statement: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University lists red spider mites (Tetranychus spp.) as a tomato pest. This source does not establish that every image in the dataset class is specifically the two-spotted species.

reported_symptoms.statement: Reported damage includes reddish-brown or bronzed leaves; severe infestation may produce silken webbing, leaf drying, and effects on flower and fruit formation.

sources.title: Target Spot of Tomato in Florida
sources.organization: University of Florida Institute of Food and Agricultural Sciences Extension

background.statement: Tomato target spot is caused by Corynespora cassiicola and occurs in tropical and subtropical regions as well as some protected-production systems.

reported_symptoms.statement: Leaf lesions may be small and necrotic with light-brown centers and dark margins; symptoms can begin within the canopy. Fruit lesions may start as slightly sunken brown flecks and develop into pitted areas.

sources.title: Leaf curl
sources.organization: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Agritech Portal

background.statement: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University describes tomato leaf curl as a virus-associated disease spread by Bemisia whiteflies and movement of infected plants. The TNAU page uses the name tomato leaf curl virus, which is not necessarily a strain-level confirmation of the dataset label TYLCV.

reported_symptoms.statement: Reported symptoms include severe stunting, downward rolling and crinkling of leaves, shortened internodes, and a bushy appearance.

sources.title: Tobacco Mosaic Virus & Tomato Mosaic Virus
sources.organization: Utah State University Extension, Plant Health / Integrated Pest Management

background.statement: Tomato mosaic virus is a tobamovirus. The cited source discusses tomato mosaic virus together with tobacco mosaic virus and describes spread by seed, handling, and contaminated tools.

reported_symptoms.statement: Reported symptoms can include light and dark green mosaic patterns, leaf or growing-point distortion, abnormal plant growth, and sometimes discolored or malformed fruit. Similar virus symptoms require careful diagnosis.
